key_insight: The paper argues that agentic visual reasoning should be judged by whether an MLLM knows when to use tools and how to use them effectively, not just by how elaborate its reasoning process looks. It reframes success around smarter tool use that improves task completion.
problem_solved: Existing agentic visual reasoning methods can be powerful but inefficient, often using tools even when they are unnecessary or using them in the wrong way. This paper addresses how to make MLLMs more adaptive and effective in deciding when and how to invoke tools for complex visual tasks.
method: Introduces two core dimensions for evaluating tool use in agentic visual reasoning: Mode Adaptiveness (when to use tools) and Tool Effect (how well tools help).
Analyzes MLLM behavior through these two lenses to distinguish unnecessary tool use from truly beneficial tool-assisted reasoning.
Proposes a framework for improving task success by aligning tool invocation with actual problem difficulty and tool utility.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a clearer way to design and evaluate agentic multimodal systems that are both more accurate and more efficient. It can help reduce wasted computation while improving performance on challenging visual reasoning tasks.

paper_title: Beacon: Knowing When and How to Perform Agentic Visual Reasoning
paper_authors: Qixun Wang, Yang Shi, Letian Cheng, Zhuoran Zhang, Yan He
